territorial_scope.description: Directs US federal executive departments and agencies; provides cybersecurity support to state and local authorities and critical-infrastructure operators.

evidence.quote: expedite and prioritize the cyber defense of civilian Federal Government information systems

summary.short: Directs federal agencies to prioritize cyber defense of national security and federal information systems, creates a Treasury-led AI cybersecurity clearinghouse, and sets up a voluntary government-access framework for frontier models before release. Bars mandatory model licensing. Directs DOJ to prioritize prosecution of AI-enabled computer crime.
summary.long: Executive order on AI-related cybersecurity and frontier-model security. Within 30 days, the Committee on National Security Systems, the Secretary of War, and DHS (through CISA) must prioritize cyber defense of national security and federal systems; DHS must issue binding operational directives and other guidance. Treasury must form an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse in voluntary collaboration with industry and critical-infrastructure operators, and OMB must assess whether federal grant funds can support AI vulnerability detection. Within 60 days, OPM must expand cybersecurity hiring pathways; Treasury, the Secretary of War, NSA, CISA, NIST and Commerce must develop a classified benchmark for designating 'covered frontier models' and a voluntary framework giving government up to 30 days' pre-release access. The order states that it authorizes no mandatory licensing, preclearance or permitting for AI model development or release. The Attorney General must prioritize enforcement of existing federal computer-crime statutes against AI-enabled unauthorized access. The order creates no enforceable rights and is subject to applicable law and appropriations.

notes: The body of the order gives no date; the 'June 2, 2026' date comes from registry metadata only. Deadlines in Secs. 2-3 run from 'the date of this order'. The 'covered frontier model' threshold in Sec. 3(a) is set through a classified benchmarking process and is not stated in the text. Sec. 3(c) disclaims any mandatory licensing or preclearance. Sec. 5(c) states that the order creates no enforceable rights. No internal inconsistencies were identified. Relations are cross-references only; the text amends, repeals, implements and transposes no other instrument.
